signature.instructions:
You are given the full text of a political fundraising email whose sponsoring committee could NOT be recovered by deterministic parsing. Return the legal name of the political committee that paid for the email, copied verbatim from the email text.

Where to look, in priority order:
1. The FEC disclaimer, usually near the bottom. It appears in forms such as 'Paid for by <COMMITTEE>', 'Paid for and authorized by <COMMITTEE>', 'Paid political advertisement paid for and provided in kind by <COMMITTEE>', or 'Authorized by <COMMITTEE>'. The committee name is everything after 'by' up to the first comma, semicolon, sentence-ending period, pipe, treasurer/officer name, mailing address (e.g. 'P.O. Box', a street number), or the start of the next sentence (such as 'not authorized by any candidate...', "Don't want to receive...", 'Click here to unsubscribe...').
2. 'Checks can be made payable to <COMMITTEE>' or 'Contributions to <COMMITTEE> are not deductible...'.
3. The organization named in the footer address block (the capitalized name directly before a P.O. Box or street address), or the sending organization in the header.

Domain knowledge and rules:
- Plain-text conversion of these emails frequently DELETES spaces, gluing words together (e.g. 'theNRSC', 'ofAmerica', 'SouthCarolina'). Restore the intended word boundaries and drop a glued leading article like 'the' if it is not part of the name.
- Committee names routinely contain middle initials with periods (e.g. 'First M. Last for <State>'); KEEP those initials and their periods — never truncate the name at an initial.
- Names often end in words like Committee, Campaign, Fund, PAC, Inc., Victory, Action, Friends of, or 'for <State/Office>'. Include the whole phrase.
- Some committees are referred to only by their well-known acronym in the disclaimer (all-capital letters). In that case return that acronym exactly as written, with no surrounding article and no trailing period.
- The name is frequently written twice in a row just before the mailing address. Report the name ONCE, with words correctly separated.
- Output ONLY the committee name: no 'Paid for by' prefix, no treasurer or officer name, no street address, no trailing punctuation, no explanation.
- Preserve the email's own spelling and capitalization. Keep a leading 'The' only if the email capitalizes it as part of the name.
- Never substitute a candidate's personal name alone, a slogan, a vendor (ActBlue, NGP VAN, ActionNetwork), or a URL when the committee name appears in the email.
- If several disclaimers appear, use the one that paid for THIS email.
